result.report:
The supplied argument establishes the two-vertex theorem for every m≥0, including the requested m=1 full two-fold contact statement. The embedded n100 product criterion also checks out with its stated rational-reference restriction on the negative direction. The original P05.2 classification remains open. Prior verdicts, hashes, compilation, and the requested conclusion were not treated as assumptions.

I checked the exact [BMPS v1 PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1), including the divisor definitions and proof bodies, and reconstructed its dependency on [Allermann–Rau Proposition 3.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0709.3705v3). The quoted [Rockafellar text](https://djvu.online/file/68u51YEBQaqiP) supports the finite-generation input explicitly invoked by n100. The main argument also supplies an independent finite-generation and elimination proof; rationality follows from its rational active equations and homogenization.

The divisor extension to real coefficients is valid. On each fixed finite rational complex, continuity and balancing impose rational linear equations. Clearing denominators permits application of the literal identities, and their polynomial dependence passes them to real coefficients and weights. Saturated quotient lattices preserve the primitive normals used in local fan calculations. Effectivity is established separately, rather than inferred from this algebraic extension.

The lift preserves every actual PCC, including those arising on other rational subdivisions: a centre at either vertex can involve only its incident strips, and an edge-interior centre only its own strip. The two local maps are unimodular onto saturated planes and agree on the bounded edge. They therefore preserve tangent lattices, primitive quotient normals, balancing, and every successive divisor coefficient. No global pushforward theorem is required.

Lemma 1's endpoint continuity and finite derivative arguments are valid. Equal-parameter vertex PCCs force all three endpoint limits to equal the vertex value and exclude negative-infinite outgoing derivatives. Convexity gives p₀≤p₁, and the two derivative-sum inequalities supply the compatible global affine supports. A harmless clarification is needed in the second-leaf sentence: for a support touching a+td, its value at a is k_d(t)−βt, where β∈∂k_d(t); it need not equal k(a). With p(a)=p₁, p(d)=β and p(e)=p₁−β, the stated vertex-swapped construction works exactly.

Lemma 2 controls arbitrary finite raw competitors. Its partial infima cannot be +∞; finiteness at one rational graph point propagates along an edge and through vertex PCCs to every rational graph point, including remote endpoints. Fibre subgradients and Lemma 1 consequently supply touching affine minorants at all rational carrier points. The positive relation among the four lifted leaves makes their expanding tetrahedra contain every ambient point eventually, proving that the supremum of supports is finite. Rational-simplex PCCs then majorize raw competitors at real points, while density preserves both continuous upper bounds. No continuity assertion about raw PC functions is used.

The epigraph construction establishes the actual envelope. Reference positivity excludes lineality in every common affine cell. The resulting finite point-and-ray representation of K is closed, has full spatial projection, and lies above the finite convex lower bound g−C. Its lower boundary H is therefore the greatest ambient convex minorant. Applying Lemma 2 to every competitor proves P=H|X, with the global bounds γ−C≤P≤γ+u≤γ+C.

The finite rational spatial conclusion is justified despite arbitrary real heights: each lower graph face projects to the convex hull and cone of selected rational spatial generators. Projection is an affine isomorphism on that face and preserves its face intersections. Restriction to the strips and pullback give the required finite rational complex. Ambient supporting planes prove effectivity against every nonnegative local real balanced cycle, in every positive dimension. Thus P is genuinely real PAPC, and P+1/j supplies decreasing uniform regularization with unchanged recursive divisors. The measure used throughout is the full d-fold zero-cycle, without removing its factorial.

Both recursive vanishing lemmas are valid on the whole local cycle. In quotient vanishing, each intersection moves support into successively higher-codimension quotient faces; on the preceding stratum the function is affine, so balancing cancels its next divisor. Common lineality gives a generalized fan with no zero-dimensional faces, and refinement cannot introduce an atom.

Every noncontact case establishes the necessary vanishing antecedent. The selected generator representation gives a nonzero rational L annihilated by active slope differences. At A, s=M_B+R+t either supplies independent b,c directions in L∩W_A or forces L into the affine factor. At B, t=s+1−M_B−R and 1−M_B−R≥0 give the corresponding d,e alternative. On the bounded-edge interior, the displayed combinations of paired leaf generators have strictly negative or positive a-component. On a leaf, the excess total parameter forces a selected outward ray or a point beyond the centre; otherwise every selected generator already lies in the local strip tangent. The lattice symmetries cover the remaining leaves. Each case yields either quotient dimension below d or common nonzero lineality. Consequently every noncontact candidate atom has zero full coefficient, including vertex-fibre and lower-face contributions. Positivity and finite atomicity prove contact support, and the bounded integrand vanishes at all remaining atoms.

I reconstructed n100's negative witnesses completely. The nine-quadrant table, all axis contributions, primitive diagonal generators and gcd normal factors give B·A=4CC′δ₀ and q²=8CC′δ₀. The direct product divisor rule introduces no additional lattice index. Its multinomial multiplicity d!/2 gives κ=2^(m+2)d!CC′e∏M_l. The zero curve supplies a genuine rational PCC after cancellation of its common scalar factor.

For each permitted rational reference, the finite recession-slope comparison proves γ≥ηρ−B. Choosing λK<η and rational M gives P=max(λQ,γ−M), with P=λQ on ρ≤2R and exactly P=γ−M sufficiently far out. All maximum walls are rational because this negative construction uses rational coefficients. The zero-curve PCC, radial chords, and same-face rational simplices bound every raw competitor by P, proving the actual envelope. Inside the obstacle roof its measure is λ^dκδ₀; outside, the integrand is zero. Hence the complete defect is −ελ^dκ. The rectangle calculation and choice of ε establish nonseparability without assuming whole-pair regularity.

The positive n100 proof also checks out independently. Its coefficient splitting establishes global rational Jensen inequalities; its ambient infimum has the stated finite lower bound using a representation of −y. The epigraph and rational-domain arguments then apply. At noncontact, s>0 forces the projection of L onto the entire star span; the other two cases give a nonzero strip tangent or affine lineality. Bivalent factors reduce to constant-weight affine lines, and the zero-dimensional endpoint case is immediate.

Two further harmless corrections concern source presentation. In Allermann–Rau's final commutativity calculation, the divisor formula also contributes −Στ λτ a(uτ)b(uτ), omitted from the displayed double sum. This term is symmetric, so retaining it proves the claimed equality; determinant indices are interpreted with inward orientation. In n100's description of BMPS Theorem 4.13, “uniform-continuous” should read “continuous for the uniform topology.” That extension theorem and Proposition 4.16 are explicitly unused. No essential step depends on analytic realization, smooth-test descent, local-to-global current ascent, separability, or an all-real-reference negative converse.

passages.statement: Let Π be a finite rational polyhedral complex in a lattice vector space N_R, with saturated tangent lattices N_σ=N∩span_R(σ−σ). For literal continuous PA functions a,b with integral tangent linear parts and rational affine constants, and a rational balanced k-cycle z with k≥1, the primitive-normal formula (a·z)(τ)=Σ_{σ≻τ}z(σ)a_{σ,lin}(n_{σ/τ})−a_{τ,lin}(Σ_{σ≻τ}z(σ)n_{σ/τ}) is lift-independent and produces a balanced (k−1)-cycle. It is compatible with rational refinement, additive in admissible PA functions, Q-linear in cycle weights, and satisfies b·(a·z)=a·(b·z) for k≥2. These constructions apply to rational generalized fans with lineality and restrictions to ordinary open subsets. (BMPS, arXiv:2603.08664v1, Definition 2.31, Remark 2.33, Lemmas 2.34–2.35, Remark 2.37.)

For a lattice Λ and an affine tropical k-cycle C in Λ⊗R represented by finite rational balanced fans with integer weights, where k≥1, every continuous piecewise affine function a with integral tangent linear parts on a fan representative defines a balanced (k−1)-cycle a·C by the primitive-normal divisor formula. For k≥2 and another such function b, b·(a·C)=a·(b·C). (Allermann–Rau, First Steps in Tropical Intersection Theory, Proposition 3.7.)

For a lattice Λ and an affine tropical k-cycle C in Λ⊗R represented by finite rational balanced fans with integer weights, where k≥1, every continuous piecewise affine function a with integral tangent linear parts on a fan representative defines a balanced (k−1)-cycle a·C by the primitive-normal divisor formula. For k≥2 and another such function b, b·(a·C)=a·(b·C). (Allermann–Rau, First Steps in Tropical Intersection Theory, Proposition 3.7.)

For a nonempty convex set C in a finite-dimensional real vector space, the following are equivalent: C is polyhedral; C is closed and has finitely many faces; C is finitely generated by points and directions. If C is closed and contains no lines, it is the convex hull of its extreme points and extreme directions in the points-and-directions convention. (Rockafellar, Convex Analysis, Theorems 18.5 and 19.1.)
